Areas above the x axis come out as positive numbers but areas under the x axis come out negative so when a problem has both cases we need to ignore the negative. There are no negative areas! Here is an explanation… Look at this sine graph… The integral from x = 0 to x = π is exactly 2 The integral from x = π to x = 2π comes out as – 2 but the real area =+2 If we Integrate from x = 0 to 2π we get 0 (ZERO) but if I asked for the area under y = sin(x) from x = 0 to x = 2π we need to ignore the negative 2 and say the area is 4 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Similarly if we integrate from x = 0 to 6π we get 2 – 2 + 2 – 2 + 2 – 2 = 0 But of course the area BETWEEN the curve and the x axis is 12. So this area from x = 0 to 6π cannot be done with one integration. It has to be done by integrating the parts above the x axis and the parts below the x axis separately. Question: Are there more counting numbers or are there more numbers between 0 and 1? There are an infinite number of counting numbers, but you can always add another decimal place to any number between 0 and 1. This question has stumped me for a while.
Answer: It is necessary to explain this as simply as possible or very few people will understand! Suppose we want to count the number of letters in the alphabet. We put them in order and pair off each letter with the counting numbers as below… Then we say that there are 26 letters in the alphabet. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Now the counting numbers never end! So this is what people mean by “they go on to infinity”. There is no last counting number. There is no last one at infinity! ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Now this seems weird but let’s try to count the even numbers… The problem is that this never comes to an end either! We say that the EVEN numbers are also never-ending (i.e. infinite) It seems logical to say there are twice as many counting numbers as there are even numbers BUT because we can pair off each even number with a counting number for ever they are BOTH INFINITE in the same way! So in a way, if some things can be paired off with the ordinary counting numbers in this never-ending way we say they are both the same infinite size! For instance, the ODD numbers are the same infinite size as the counting numbers too! —————————————————————————————————————- Even the rational numbers (fractions) can be shown to be paired off with the counting numbers. (I will show you how in a link below). So all these sets of numbers are the same infinite size! However, when we think of all numbers including irrational numbers on a line, it can be shown that we cannot pair them off with the natural counting numbers! So this would be a set which is a bigger type of infinite number! In brief, the number of numbers between 0 and 1 is uncountable because they can’t be paired off with the natural counting numbers. (I can also show you how in a link below). The weird idea is that there are different sizes of infinity! ----------------------------------------------------------------------- Click on this link and scroll to my answer.

Question: Can calculus be learned without being taught how to solve equations by hand? Is using a calculator allowed in learning calculus?
Answer: “Knowing formulas” or “using calculators that do algebra and solve problems” are not the same as “understanding mathematics”. There is a big difference between “knowing a thing” and “understanding it”. People who are good at mathematics do not look at a problem and say to themselves “What formula do I use to solve this?” or “What artificial intelligence app shall I use to do this?” People who are good at mathematics use logical techniques or methods to solve problems not formulas or rules or websites that answer their questions. Good teachers carefully go through the proper reasoning for essential basic concepts and yet a disappointingly large proportion of students simply wait until the “formula” appears then simply apply the formula without understanding where it came from, despite the teacher’s best intentions! I believe students need to appreciate the logic in mathematics otherwise they are just blindly following rules. Some people actually believe that mathematics is just a whole lot of rules and if you know the rules, you will be good at mathematics! Mathematics is completely logical and if you follow the logic it is enjoyable, exciting and very satisfying! When I teach junior classes, I don’t just say “What is the formula for the area of a triangle? I give out rewards for people who can explain WHY it is base times height, divided by 2. When I teach more senior classes I don’t just say “What does sine squared theta plus cos squared theta equal?” I say “Who can explain WHY it equals 1?” Then we proceed to use it in some problem. Actually, a favourite question of mine when teaching a new senior class is this: “What is 2 to the power zero?” Everyone “knows” it is 1. Then I say, “Who can explain WHY it is 1?” Hardly anyone can! It is then that I find out those people who just wait for the “rule” and carry on using it without understanding why! They soon find out that in my classes they have to understand why things are what they are and not just remember rules and results! I could go on for hours on this topic but if you are into this concept please look at a special website I wrote about this.
